confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches. One was for the RBA exchange rate and two were for Chania prices. Most price data comes from crowd-sourced and aggregator sites with mixed dates. Those sites put a cappuccino at about EUR 3.0-3.6, a 0.5L local beer at about EUR 4.0-4.5, a budget meal at about EUR 13-15, mid-range dinner for two at about EUR 50 and a downtown cocktail at about EUR 9. One site said its cocktail figure is not yet reliable. A 2026 Chania harbour guide says beer or house wine costs EUR 7-10 on the waterfront. I nudged the figures up a little for July high season and tourist areas, but I did not use waterfront premium prices as typical. I estimated the cocktail at about EUR 10 from the EUR 9 aggregator figure and a Rethymno range of EUR 8-13. Wine-by-the-glass figures from undated venue menus and guides varied widely, from about EUR 5 to EUR 12. I used about EUR 6, which is moderately uncertain. I converted EUR to USD at about 1.10, the cross rate implied by the RBA's 18 Nov 2026 AUD rates (0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR). The accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge, not from any search or listing. Chania has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel figures are especially uncertain. All accommodation figures assume July peak-season rates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink figures are Chania-specific aggregator values, checked against Rethymno, a nearby city on Crete. The accommodation figures are based on mid-sized Greek island tourist towns in peak season, such as Rethymno and Heraklion. They should be cheaper than Santorini or Mykonos and somewhat higher than mainland Greek cities like Thessaloniki.
